subject: Prod path: latency / QPS handoff & recommendation

Subject: Prod path: latency / QPS handoff & recommendation

Hi Ellen — thanks again for a really helpful call this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we’re aligned.

Summary of FastCart workload (as discussed)
- Steady-state: ~30 QPS (concurrent user-driven requests)
- Peak bursts: up to ~220 QPS for ~30–90s during checkout surges
- Average tokens per request (input + expected output): ~280 tokens (mostly short JSON responses)
- Delivery requirement: p95 ~120ms, p99 target <=400ms for checkout flows; streaming not required for this integration
- Sensitive data: payment token references and PII — customer would prefer VPC or dedicated isolation for PCI scope work (security team to confirm)

Redwood options and our read:
1) Hosted API — fastest path to production; seamless autoscaling for bursts but less control over reserved capacity; good if FastCart can tolerate occasional higher tail variance and wants minimal ops.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) — predictable throughput at low tail variance, can meet p99 targets during sustained traffic; recommended if you want guaranteed unblock for peak bursts without fallback latency spikes.
3) Private VPC / on-prem — strong for regulated workloads; higher setup time and procurement. We’d do this if FastCart needs isolation/KMS in your cloud account.

Our recommendation (based on target p99 <=400ms + large short bursts): start with a 2-week Dedicated pilot with overflow routing to Hosted for extreme bursts. That gives you predictable SLOs while limiting initial setup friction. If Security requires it after pilot, we can discuss VPC onboarding.

As next steps:
- Can you share a short QPS/time CSV (a one-week sample) so we can size the Dedicated pool? (I attached a template: fastcart_token_profile.csv)
- Ben will draft a two-week Dedicated pilot SOW with success criteria (p95/p99, warm-up profile, rollback conditions).
- Rajiv / Security: can you confirm whether PCI-scope data will require customer-managed KMS or if token references are sufficient?

I’ve cc’d Ben (pilot SOW) and Marissa (customer success / SLA). If that plan sounds OK I’ll schedule a short kickoff for Wednesday.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu

Subject: Re: Prod path: latency / QPS handoff & recommendation

Thanks Jasmine — that recap looks right. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The p99 <=400ms is critical for checkout confirmation; we’ll tolerate occasional edge cases but want the pilot to demonstrate stability under flash sale patterns.
- Typical payload is closer to 320 tokens if you include metadata. Most calls are independent (not prefix cacheable).
- We would prefer Dedicated for predictable customer experience, but we need clarity on how overflow to Hosted is handled (do we keep session affinity? will tokens be routed to a different model variant?).
- Procurement: we prefer a short pilot SOW and then commit to a 6–12 month reserved capacity if the pilot meets SLOs — send the SOW to procurement@fastcart.com.

I’ll attach a 48-hour QPS export after I’m back at my desk. Rajiv will follow up on whether tokens are considered PCI within our implementation.

— Ellen

Folks — forwarding Ellen’s reply. Key asks: Dedicated pilot (2 weeks) with overflow to Hosted. Procurement wants the SOW and Rajiv will confirm PCI scope.

My suggested approach:
- Ben: draft a 2-week Dedicated pilot SOW (deliverables: infra sizing, canary traffic plan, p95/p99 targets, monitoring hooks, rollback policy). Include a short test harness that replays FastCart’s 48h QPS sample for verification.
- Marissa: please prepare minimal SLA language for pilot acceptance and a checklist for cutover to reserved capacity (if pilot successful).
- I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff once Ben has the SOW draft.

Also, flagging we should call out overflow behavior: plan is to keep session affinity where possible and route to a compatible model variant; fallback must be documented in the SOW.

-J

Subject: Re: Prod path: latency / QPS handoff & recommendation — Dedicated pilot SOW and next steps

Hi Ellen — great to meet you on the call. Per Jasmine’s note, I’ve attached a short pilot SOW and a template for the QPS export (fastcart_token_profile.csv). Summary below:

Pilot scope (2 weeks)
- Dedicated GPU pool sized for steady 30 QPS + 4x burst capacity (sustained 220 QPS for up to 2 minutes)
- Success criteria: p95 <= 150ms and p99 <= 400ms on checkout endpoints for three representative test windows
- Observability: route-level latency breakdown, token-level cost, and live tracing to reproduce tail spikes
- Overflow behavior: requests beyond the Dedicated pool will be routed to Hosted API with documented model variant mapping; session affinity will be preserved via request key where applicable

Attachments provided: redwood_dedicated_pilot_sow.pdf, fastcart_token_profile.csv
Next steps:
1) Ellen / Rajiv: send the 48h QPS export (CSV) and confirm PCI question — if tokens are not in-scope we proceed as normal; if they are, we’ll add KMS/VPC steps and adjust timeline.
2) Procurement: sign the pilot SOW (DocuSign link will follow).
3) We’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff within 2 business days of sign-off and provision the Dedicated pool immediately after SOW execution.
